newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Feb M2 supply rises 19.6 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Feb M2 supply rises 19.6 pct on year.

text.p: South Korea's M2 money supply rose 19.6 percent year-on-year in February, against a 14.8 percent rise a year earlier, provisional Bank of Korea (BOK) figures showed on Thursday.
Note - M2 consists of money in circulation, and checking and savings account deposits with banks. MCT includes banks' trust account savings and certificates of deposit on top of M2.
The central bank said in a statement the M2 rise in February was higher than a year earlier because of a deposit shift in banks from trust accounts to savings accounts.
Central bank officials said money in trust accounts had fallen steadily since May 1996, when the maturity was extended by up to six months from one year.
"Deposits in trust accounts dropped to 1.6 trillion won in February from 3.2 trillion won a year ago," said Ahn Koo-yong, assistant director at the central bank's money market division.
"But the money supply measured in MCT fell, reflecting stability in the money market," he said.

The central bank said it saw no signs of excessive liquidity in February despite an injection of funds to meet rising money demand for the Lunar New Year and to counter possible shortages after the Hanbo Steel failure.
Savings account deposits with banks rose to 2.3 trillion won in February from 1.4 trillion a year before, the bank said.
Repayments for certificates for deposits (CDs) in February were 1.5 trillion won higher than issues in the month. A year ago, CD repayments outstripped issues by 163 billion won.
